correctness.rationale: An injective choice of colours by parts proves Z_{m,q}=sum_s binom(m,s)(q)_{2m-s}. The within-pair equality probability is exactly q Z_{m-1,q-1}/Z_{m,q}. Full S_q symmetry forces colour-frequency orthogonality and determines both kinds of spatial off-diagonal entry. Antipodal, pair-average-contrast, and total vectors give an exhaustive orthogonal 2m-dimensional eigenbasis, for each of the q-1 Fourier frequencies. Positivity at q>m follows from p<1 and the inequality p> (2m-q)/q when m<q<2m; at q>=2m it is immediate. At q=m the exact nullity follows from p=1. At q=m+1 direct count yields p=m/(m+1), hence condition ratio 2m+1. At fixed m, conditional available-palette bounds yield p=1/q+O_m(q^-2), proving the asymptotic. The new checker passed 242 exact-rational block cases, eight direct colouring enumerations, 3756 independently assembled full-complex-Fourier Gram-entry checks, and high-palette consistency tests. Finite computations corroborate, but do not prove, the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary graph-colouring literature gives chromatic enumerators, weighted-colouring partition functions, or complete-multipartite symmetric-function decompositions, not the full site-character Gram spectrum and sharp first-extra-colour Riesz ratio on cross-polytope graphs. A prior complete-bipartite colouring-frame result covers m=2 only; the present claim requires m>=3. Relevant published-result searches returned no statement implication giving the q>=m+1 rank theorem and three explicit nonconstant eigenlevels for this graph family. This is bounded evidence of originality, not proof of priority.
residual_risks: A prior Potts two-point-correlation or random-colouring association-scheme calculation could express this same special spectrum under different terminology. Search results do not prove uniqueness.
The graph-colouring primary sources were inspected in relevant sections; not every page of every longer work was read.

value.rationale: The graph is the 1-skeleton of the classical cross-polytope and models a palette-constrained zero-temperature Potts ensemble. The natural all-one-site Fourier band has a sharp rank transition: a large forced nullspace at exactly the chromatic palette q=m, then complete independence at the first extra colour q=m+1 with the exact growing worst-to-best energy ratio 2m+1. The complete three-sector spectrum and high-palette flattening quantify reconstruction stability on every graph dimension and palette. Neither a single small instance nor merely a known chromatic count is asserted as the contribution; the all-parameter Riesz bounds are the motivated invariant.
